task_title: Add the Supabase read repository/API and wire it through the mobile repository interface
result: PASS — published-only read API added, adapter wired at the composition root, all SQL and mobile tests pass.
user_visible_outcome: No screen change. The app now has a published-content read repository (port + store + Supabase adapter) injected by the composition root, reading the published-only public_content views. Unconfigured or failing backends return an honest empty result instead of crashing.
files_changed: supabase/migrations/20260915000013_published_read_api.sql (new: stable client keys in the published views; structural read grants/policies)
apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx (wire initializePublishedContent in the configured branch)

read_api.published_attestations: entity_key, scope_key, reference_local_key, kind, explicitness, review_state
read_api.published_verses: edition_key, refsys_key, book_osis, chapter, verse_number, local_key, text, text_sha256
read_api.security: Every view remains published-only (published package / review_state = published / edition status = published) and runs with security_invoker, so Postgres RLS decides visibility. Draft rows are never exposed. Only the public anon key is used; no service_role key and no writes.
read_api.why_views_changed: The earlier views exposed surrogate uuids and no book reference, so a client could not address rows. The read API now exposes stable client-safe keys and the structural canon columns (book OSIS, reference keys) needed to map published rows to app references.

structural_read_change: Migration 13 grants anon/authenticated read on the non-draft structural canon tables (scripture_works, reference_systems, reference_units, scripture_scopes) with permissive policies, because the security_invoker views join them. canons, memberships, mappings and all content tables stay private.

mobile_wiring.store: src/content/publishedContentStore.ts (initializePublishedContent / setPublishedContentRepository / resetPublishedContentStore / fetchPublished*); reads never throw and return [] when unconfigured or failing
mobile_wiring.adapter: src/infrastructure/supabase/publishedContentRepository.ts; depends on a narrow PublishedContentClient structural subset so tests inject a fake with no network; only module allowed to read public_content besides auth/bookmark adapters
mobile_wiring.composition_root: app/_layout.tsx calls initializePublishedContent only inside the isSyncConfigured + url/key branch, alongside auth and sync

commands_executed.command: clean rebuild: createdb bible_clean; bootstrap + migrations 01-13; REQUIRE_SUPABASE_TESTS=1 DATABASE_URL=... sh tools/verify-supabase.sh
apps/mobile: npx tsc --noEmit && npx prettier --check . && npx jest
commands_executed.output: 31 suites, 270 tests passed; 0 eslint errors (17 warnings, below baseline)

commands_executed.command: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test

tests.sql_09: Seeds a published package/edition + published and draft attestations, then proves anon and authenticated see exactly the published verse/attestation with stable keys, and never the draft rows.
tests.mobile: published-content.test.ts proves the adapter issues the exact view/column/filter reads and maps rows, propagates backend errors, and that the store is safe when unconfigured, failing, or initialized from injected deps.

known_limitations: Reads return published rows only; nothing is published yet, so the read API yields empty results in practice until a publication release exists. Drafts intentionally stay invisible.
The mobile store is not yet consumed by any screen (no screen change was requested); it is wired at the composition root and proven by tests.
No new dependency was added; @supabase/supabase-js 2.116.0 was already present.
A live Supabase-hosted confirmation (supabase db reset + hosted run) has not been performed here.
stop_condition: Stopped after the read repository/API is implemented, wired through the repository pattern, and proven by SQL and mobile tests. No publication, no anonymous draft exposure, no screen redesign.
